title: Interview Execution
purpose: Perform under interview conditions, gated by readiness.

units.title: Interview execution
units.purpose: Clarify, reason, implement, test, debug, explain: under a clock, without help.

reps.title: Count with .get
reps.prompt: Write `count_words(words)` returning a dict that maps each word to how many times it appears. Use `.get`, no `Counter`.

reps.title: Trace first-seen indexes
reps.prompt: What does this print?

reps.title: Last index of each value
reps.prompt: Write `last_seen(nums)` returning a dict that maps each value to the **last** index where it appears.

reps.title: Pass the parcel
reps.prompt: Players sit in a circle in the order of `names`. Each pass moves the front player to the back. Return who is at the front after `passes` passes. Use a `deque`.

reps.title: pop(0) in a loop
reps.prompt: A deque takes from the front with `popleft()`. Why not a list and `pop(0)`? Time complexity of this for n numbers?

reps.title: k smallest with heapq
reps.prompt: Write `k_smallest(nums, k)` returning the `k` smallest values in ascending order, using `heapq` push and pop. Assume `0 <= k <= len(nums)`.

reps.title: Trace a heap of tuples
reps.prompt: What does this print?

reps.title: Sort by length, then alphabet
reps.prompt: Write `by_length(words)` returning the words sorted shortest first, ties broken alphabetically. One line.

reps.title: Slices
reps.prompt: What does this print?

reps.title: Leaderboard
reps.prompt: `scores` maps name → score. Return the names, highest score first; equal scores in alphabetical order.

reps.title: In-bounds neighbors
reps.prompt: `grid` is a non-empty list of equal-length rows. Return the in-bounds neighbors of cell `(r, c)` (the cells directly up, down, left and right of it) as a list of `(row, col)` tuples in the order up, down, left, right.

reps.title: Character counts
reps.prompt: Return a dict mapping each character of `s` to how many times it appears.

reps.title: Pair sum, one pass
reps.prompt: Return the indexes `[i, j]` (with `i < j`) of two numbers that add to `target`, in one pass. Return `[]` if there is no pair.

reps.title: Search the sorted list
reps.prompt: Return the index of `target` in the sorted list `nums`, or -1 if it is absent. O(log n).

reps.title: Reverse a linked list
reps.prompt: Reverse the linked list in place and return the new head.

reps.title: Sum a tree
reps.prompt: Return the sum of all node values in the binary tree. An empty tree sums to 0.

reps.title: Count reachable cells
reps.prompt: `grid` has `0` for open cells and `1` for walls. Starting from the open cell `(r, c)`, return how many open cells can be reached moving up, down, left or right (including the start). Each cell must be counted once.

reps.title: All subsets
reps.prompt: Return every subset of `nums` (distinct numbers). The order of subsets does not matter.

reps.title: k largest
reps.prompt: Return the `k` largest values, largest first, using a min-heap that never holds more than `k` items (O(n log k)). `1 <= k <= len(nums)`.

reps.title: Merge meetings
reps.prompt: Merge overlapping (or touching) intervals given in any order. Return the merged intervals sorted by start. Input is non-empty.

reps.title: Merge two sorted lists
reps.prompt: Merge two sorted linked lists into one sorted list and return its head.

reps.title: Longest run without repeats
reps.prompt: Return the length of the longest substring of `s` with no repeated characters, in one pass.

reps.title: Brute force to optimal
reps.prompt: Prompt: "Given an unsorted list of numbers and a target, return the indexes of two numbers that add to the target." Before any code, say out loud how you get from the obvious solution to the best one. Then write it down.

reps.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters (cold)
reps.prompt: Cold rep. No scaffolding — write it from a blank editor. `s` is a string. Return the length of the longest stretch of consecutive characters in which no character appears twice. The stretch must be unbroken. In `"pwwkew"

reps.title: Justify the window
reps.prompt: The interviewer says: "There is a loop inside a loop, so this is O(n^2), right?" Answer out loud, then write your answer: time and space, and why.

reps.title: Dry-run out loud
reps.prompt: A set-based version of the window you just wrote. Trace it on `"abba"` the way you would for an interviewer: after each character, say `left`, the set, and `best`.

reps.prompt: Cold rep. No scaffolding — write it from a blank editor. `s` is a string made only of the six characters `( ) [ ] { }`. Return `True` if `s` is well formed, otherwise `False`. It is well formed when all of these hold: -

reps.prompt: You just counted islands. Assume a traversal from every unvisited land cell, marking cells visited when queued. Time complexity on an R × C grid?

reps.title: Justify a graph traversal
reps.prompt: State the time and space of this function in terms of n courses and e prerequisite pairs, and justify each term.

reps.title: Most frequent k values (cold)
reps.prompt: Cold rep. No scaffolding — write it from a blank editor. Given a list of integers `nums` and an integer `k`, return the `k` values that occur most often. Return them in any order. You may assume the answer is unique (no

reps.prompt: Cold rep. No scaffolding — write it from a blank editor. You get a list of ranges, each `[start, end]` with `start <= end`, in no particular order. Combine every group of ranges that overlap (ranges that only touch at an

reps.title: Clarifying questions
reps.prompt: You just merged intervals from a blank editor. In the real interview the first two minutes come before the code: write the clarifying questions you would ask for "combine overlapping time ranges", and the inputs you woul

reps.title: Every subset (cold)
reps.prompt: Cold rep. No scaffolding — write it from a blank editor. Given a list `nums` of distinct integers, return every possible subset (the power set), including the empty one and `nums` itself. No subset may appear twice. The

reps.title: All subsets
reps.prompt: You just generated every subset. Time complexity of this version for n numbers?

reps.title: No two neighbours (cold)
reps.prompt: Cold rep. No scaffolding — write it from a blank editor. A row of houses each holds some non-negative amount of cash, given as `nums`. You may collect from any houses you like, except that you may never collect from two

reps.title: Memoized recursion
reps.prompt: You just solved a one-dimensional DP bottom-up. Here is the top-down version of a similar recurrence: time complexity of `ways(n)`?

reps.title: Nearby repeat
reps.prompt: Return `True` if some value appears at two different positions `i` and `j` with `abs(i - j) <= k`.

reps.title: Make it linear
reps.prompt: This returns the items of `a` that also appear in `b`, in the order of `a` (repeats in `a` kept). It is O(n·m) because `x in b` scans a list. Rewrite it to run in O(n + m) with the same output.

reps.title: Squares in order
reps.prompt: `nums` is sorted ascending and may contain negatives. Return the squares of the numbers, sorted ascending, in O(n) without calling sort.

reps.title: At most two kinds
reps.prompt: Return the length of the longest contiguous stretch of `items` that contains at most two distinct values.

reps.title: First position at least target
reps.prompt: `nums` is sorted ascending (duplicates allowed). Return the first index `i` with `nums[i] >= target`, or `len(nums)` if there is none. O(log n).

reps.title: Root-to-leaf total
reps.prompt: Return `True` if some path from the root down to a **leaf** has values adding up to `target`. An empty tree has no paths.

reps.title: Space of tree recursion
reps.prompt: Your path-sum solution recursed down the tree with no extra data structure. Extra space used by this function (n nodes, height h)?

reps.title: Closest k points
reps.prompt: Given points `[x, y]`, return the `k` points closest to `(0, 0)` as a list of `[x, y]` lists, in any order. Aim for better than sorting everything when k is small. Assume there are no distance ties at the cut-off.

reps.title: Size-k heap
reps.prompt: You just kept a size-k heap for the closest points. Same shape here: n numbers, heap capped at size k. Time complexity?

reps.title: Count friend groups
reps.prompt: There are `n` people labeled `0..n-1`. Each pair in `edges` are friends (both ways). Friends of friends are in the same group. How many groups are there?

reps.title: Cheapest climb
reps.prompt: You stand before a staircase. `cost[i]` is what you pay when you step **off** step `i`. You may start on step 0 or step 1, and each move goes up 1 or 2 steps. Return the minimum total cost to reach the top, just past the

reps.title: Pick k of n
reps.prompt: Return every way to choose `k` distinct numbers from `1..n`, each as an ascending list. The order of the lists does not matter.

reps.title: Fewest steps through a maze
reps.prompt: `grid` has `0` for open cells and `1` for walls. Moving up, down, left or right, return the fewest moves from the top-left cell to the bottom-right cell, or `-1` if it cannot be reached (including when either corner is a

reps.title: When you are stuck
reps.prompt: You have a working O(n^2) solution and no idea how to improve it. Write what you would say and do in the next three minutes instead of going silent.
